previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including type 1 diabetes, pancreas and kidney transplants, end-stage renal disease on peritoneal dialysis, and chronic heart failure was admitted for acute anemia and hypotension. She presented with a rapid drop in hematocrit from 24 to 19, lightheadedness, and chronic symptoms including daily nosebleeds, hand rash, and nail changes. She received three units of packed red blood cells, and her pancytopenia was attributed to immunosuppressive therapy with mycophenolate mofetil (CellCept), which was discontinued. An esophageal ulcer was found on EGD and treated with increased omeprazole, while colonoscopy revealed ischemic colitis likely due to recurrent hypotension. Dermatology evaluated her painful hand rash and thickened nails, initiated urea cream, and performed a biopsy pending further evaluation. Her warfarin was held due to epistaxis and restarted at discharge after 24 hours without bleeding. Levothyroxine was increased for elevated TSH. She stabilized hemodynamically, remained euvolemic, and was discharged to extended care with plans for outpatient follow-up in hematology, gastroenterology, and dermatology to monitor pending test results and medication management.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ with DM type ___ ___ pancreas transplant, CABG, prior NSTEMIs, 
CHF, ESRD with failed renal transplants and now on PD, CHF, 
orthostatic hypotension on midodrine and fludrocortisone, and 
recent admission prior for hypotension and anemia, who presented 
with fatigue and weakness; was found to have diffuse DVTs.  
  
#DVT: Noted on ultrasound in ED after presenting with weakness 
(generalized) and fatigue for past 5 days, and was started on 
heparin drip.  Of note was off warfarin last admission for 
recurrent epistaxis and for GI bleed (found to have ischemic 
colitis and esophageal ulcer).  No CTA was done as pt was not 
complaining of dyspnea, was not tachycardic, EKG did not show R 
heart strain and no signs of PE on CXR. As a CTA was not going 
to change management, further imaging was deferred and pt 
remained hemodynamically stable without signs of obtructive 
shock due to PE. Pt's left thigh tenderness resolved on ___ 
and swelling in lower extremities remained stable. Warfarin was 
started on Hospital Day 2 at home dose of 2mg in addition to 
heparin drip and INR was therapeutic for first time on ___. 

#Fatigue and Generalized Weakness: Etiology unclear, but may be 
related to diarrhea, poor PO intake, and her multiple chronic 
medical issues. Anemia, electrolyte imbalance and 
hypothyroidism, C. diff colitis were on differential. Hct 
remained near baseline, and had no focal signs of infection, but 
is on immune suppression for her pancreas transplant. TSH 
elevated during last admission at 32, now at 6 (levothyroxine 
dose was not changed during course). Her electrolytes were 
repleted as needed and fatigue persisted. As her PO intake 
became the major issue, it appears her malnutrition was the most 
likely cause of her fatigue and weakness. C. difficile infection 
was less likely as pt was constipated during course and stool 
specimen was sent out until ___ after pt was able to pass 
stool which showed C. diff PCR positivity. Pt was then started 
on PO vancomycin and her fatigue and nausea improved.

#C. difficile colitis: Pt had diarrhea before admission and took 
Imodium religiously which masked diarrhea upon admission. On 
Hospital Day 5 pt began having diarrhea and then dx with C. 
difficile. Pt's nausea greatly improved after starting 
vancomycin 125mg q6h PO, Day ___. She is to complete a two 
week course.
 
#Peritoneal Dialysis:  Pt was seen immediately by renal 
transplant team and her peritoneal dialysate was adjusted to 
least concentrated dialysate to keep intravascular space 
repleted, and thus maintain adequate pressures. Pt remained 
anuric at baseline throughout course and had no complications 
with dialysis. Her creatinine continued to be stable at 6.
  
#Chronic Hypotension: She has chronic hypotension for which she 
is on both Midodrine and Fludrocortisone. Pt's BP ranged from 
high ___ to low 100s while on peritoneal dialysis. Per renal 
transplant recs, pt was started on NaCl PO tabs BID as she had 
poor PO intake throughout course.

#Acute on chronic anemia: Baseline Hct seems to be high ___ 
since last admission in ___. On ___ pt's hct acutely dropped 
to 20 along with worsening thrombocytopenia. She received 1u of 
RBCs then and Hct responded appropriately, and has been stable 
since without repeat transfusions. No signs of acute bleeding 
and had guiac negative stool.  Peripheral smear ___ showed no 
significant number of schistoctytes. Differential included 
hemolysis (?mechanical from valve repair) especially since pt 
with elevated LDH, and decreased haptoglobin; presentation was 
not concerning for DIC/TTP with increased platelets and normal 
fibrinogen, and pt continued to mentate at baseline. Pt's 
abnormal CBC on ___ showed acute elevation of MCV as well and 
hematology was consulted to study peripheral smears on ___ and 
___. Per heme, no concerning cells, and did see cells consistent 
with renal disease (burr cells, acanthocytes).

#Poor hand-eye-coordination, worsening tremor: Pt concerned for 
worsening resting tremor and poor hand-eye-coordination and what 
seems to be tactile proprioception issues for past 2 months. She 
was unable to have outpt neuro appt as she has been frequently 
hospitalized. Neurology was consulted and saw pt. After 
evaluation, the neuro team had no recommendations for emergent 
intervention especially pt has multiple comorbidities being 
dealt with. MRI of head was recommended by neurology which ruled 
out acute or subacute stroke, as well as mass or hemorrhage. 
Pt's diabetic neuropathy and glaucoma were most likely the main 
components to pt's poor proprioception of upper extremities.

# ___ Pancreas Transplant: Pt was continued on tacrolimus and 
prednisone as well as prophylactic medications: acylcovir and 
fluconazole. Creon was continued and Cellcept was continued to 
be held as this was postulated as the cause of pt's pancytopenia 
in past.

#Poor PO intake, malnutrition: Pt has had decreased appetite 
with fatigue with some nausea component. Standing simethicone 
was given for nausea management and salt tabs were given to 
maintain pressure while pt had poor PO intake. Nutrition was 
consulted and had difficulty recommending supplements as pt has 
intolerance to soy and lactose. Pt will need follow-up with PCP 
to discuss whether repeat EGD should be done to evaluate 
interval change in esophageal ulcer and evaluate for gastric 
outlet obstruction or gastroparesis.

# Glaucoma: Most likely related to diabetes, stable. Pt's 
decreased visual acuity was not related to her neurologic 
complaints of poor hand-eye-coordination. She was continued on 
glaucoma eye drops and artificial tears.  

Transitional issues:

___
-Pt is to follow-up with nephrologist as outpatient for further

-Pt is to follow-up with her hematologist for monitoring of
